answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic terrace of its recent computational trace on the ledger; the trace is a thread of signed opal‑colored hashes linking every inference step to a unique hardware nonce. When a new request arrives, the network recomputes the trace and rejects any output whose thread duplicates an existing terrace within a similarity margin, effectively nullifying Sybil replicas. An attacker must generate a distinct hardware‑bound nonce and produce a full, non‑duplicate computational trace for every fake identity, inflating cost linearly with the number of identities.
